subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Which public provider-family fallback contract should OpenClaw support for text agent failover: wildcard/auto refs, grouped `fallbackFamilies`, catalog-derived fallbacks, or no new fallback surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but each option creates a different public config contract and provider-routing behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design one canonical fallback contract
options.body: Adopt one provider-family fallback design and land it across schema, normalization, runtime fallback construction, availability checks, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to catalog-derived fallbacks
options.body: Use the direction from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/60922 and leave wildcard/auto and `fallbackFamilies` out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep explicit fallbacks only
options.body: Document explicit `fallbacks` as the supported path and close this feature request as not planned if the added config surface is not worth it.

recommendation.title: Design one canonical fallback contract
recommendation.body: Adopt one provider-family fallback design and land it across schema, normalization, runtime fallback construction, availability checks, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is central ownership of model fallback resolution, model config, and fallback docs.
